 BPBD DKI prepares 403 evacuation locations, 200 RW threatened by floods during the peak of the rain 
 08 November 2026, 15:00 | Editorial Team 
 Diah Ayu Wardani 
 Reporter 
 Nizar Zulmi 
 Editor 
 (Photo: special doc) 
 Share:
 JAKARTA - The DKI Jakarta Regional Disaster Management Agency (BPBD) has prepared 403 evacuation locations to anticipate flooding during the peak of the rainy season in February 2027. A total of 200 RW in Jakarta are included in the mapping of flood-prone areas.
 The threat of flooding is expected to increase when heavy rain hits Jakarta for a long duration, especially if it is accompanied by water supplies from upstream areas and sea level rise due to tides.
 The Head of the DKI Jakarta BPBD, Marulitua Sijabat, said that his party had prepared a number of handling scenarios to face the worst possibility during the peak of the rainy season.
 "We have prepared 403 evacuation locations," Marulitua said in a statement, Sunday, November 8.
 Based on the BPBD mapping, 200 RW that are prone to flooding are spread across several areas of Jakarta. Some areas that have often been affected by flooding include Cawang, Cililitan, Kampung Melayu, and Rawa Buaya.
 BPBD estimates that the intensity of rainfall in February 2027 has the potential to be very high, even extreme for a long time. This condition can trigger puddles at a number of points until it develops into a flood, especially if the capacity of the water channel is not able to accommodate the increased water discharge.
 To anticipate this condition, the DKI Provincial Government has begun to intensify cross-agency coordination. A number of parties involved include the TNI, Polri, and the Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG).
 "Including cross-sectoral coordination in the ranks of the local government has been carried out as an anticipation of the disaster situation during the peak of the rainy season," he said.
 At the regional level, the head of the sub-district and the head of the village are also asked to be involved in flood prevention efforts. The steps taken include socialization to residents, cleaning of water channels, draining channels, to improving water resources infrastructure.
 In addition to anticipating flooding, BPBD also prepares equipment to support evacuation and handling of affected residents. Equipment that is alerted includes rubber boats, evacuation tents, mobile toilets, lighting, and post tents and their operational equipment.
 Early warning systems (EWS) will also be activated to provide information to residents if there is a potential for extreme weather. Notifications are also delivered via SMS blast and digital television based on warning information from BMKG.
 BPBD will also shift supporting equipment to areas that are potentially affected before the flood occurs. Joint officers are prepared to be on standby at vulnerable points after the early warning is issued.
 "We have prepared 403 evacuation locations. They have also coordinated technically and operationally in the field," he concluded.
